name: tercel
text:
That “115.0 seconds past every synchronous read timeout” line is the kicker. It means your deep-scan flow is definitively in “this must be async” territory: any SDK or HTTP client with the usual 30–60s ceiling will hit its own wall before the work is done, even though the backend is still happily grinding away.

That directly implies one thing: protocol choice becomes a product decision, not an infra detail. If a team insists on blocking message/send semantics for work that looks like your 5-pass, 75–115s scan, they’re basically choosing failure modes and retry storms up front.

Things I’d be curious to measure next, given your data:


For the 95.0s orchestrated review: how much of that is A2A versus AG-UI overhead versus discovery (ListAgentRuntimes + GetAgentCard)?

With ten microVM-backed sessions: what’s the cold-start vs warm path latency distribution, and does the X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id pattern introduce any hot-spotting?

On the MCP side pinned to m7g.large / c7g.large: is tool latency meaningfully different from the serverless default at low QPS, or is this mostly about predictable CPU/MEM envelopes?


Also, your registry + RAM setup quietly answers a nasty org problem: “Who owns what agent/tool?” The fact that “payment processing” semantically hits billing suggests you could start tracking drift: when team naming diverges too far from how requesters describe tasks, does search relevance degrade?

name: Pin Xiong
text:
Thanks for the close read — "protocol choice is a product decision" is a sharper framing than the one I used, and I think it's right. A team that picks blocking message/send for a 75–115s workload has made a product call whether they realize it or not.

On your three questions, here is what I actually measured versus what I did not:


Breakdown of the 95.0s: I only timed it end to end. The transcript shows discovery (ListAgentRuntimes) and the agent card fetch happen once per run before the A2A call, and the specialists' LLM reasoning clearly dominates, but I did not instrument per-phase timing. Worth doing — a follow-up run with timestamps around discovery, card fetch, and each A2A hop would quantify it.
Cold vs warm: the ten-session run was designed to prove isolation (10/10 codewords recalled correctly), not latency distribution. The 88.3s for 20 invocations averages about 4.4s per call, but I did not split store versus recall or instrument for hot-spotting on the session-id pattern. No visible anomalies at this sample size, but that is an absence of measurement, not evidence of absence.
MCP pinned vs serverless default: no control group. The two data points I have are 72.5s on a freshly redeployed runtime versus 52.5s warm, which suggests cold start dominates the first call. I pinned m7g.large/c7g.large for predictable CPU/MEM envelopes, exactly the reason you guessed — whether latency differs meaningfully from the default at low QPS is still an open measurement.


The naming-drift idea is the most interesting one here. "payment processing" semantically hitting billing is exactly the mechanism, and relevance degrading as team naming diverges from requester vocabulary is testable — add a deliberately misnamed record and watch where search rank falls off. If I run that experiment, I will write it up.

If you instrument any of these on your side first, I would genuinely like to see the numbers.
